messages.subject: nimbleModel() run time
parts:
Hello Nimblers, 

I am trying to code a hierarchical resource selection function with random effects for individual and population. I've got a code that I think makes sense, and I believe I'v organized the data appropriately. But, when I run nimbleModel() on the model code, constants, and inits it essentially stalls at the calculate stage and runs for several hours, and I'm not sure if it will ever finish. I've pasted the code below, but essentially my goal is to estimate the population (wildlife management unit - WMU) level beta estimates, but because the process of selection is at the individual level I've included those betas in the likelihood. I intend to include a number of covariates, but here I am testing with a single covariate of canopy cover. I know the warning about indexing over gamma isnt ideal, but since it doesnt have a w on the right side I didnt think it really needs to be indexed over both w and i. 
I'm not sure where to start, to try and solve this. Ultimately I hope to include more than 400 deer and more than one covariate, so I am hoping I can figure things out with this smaller dataset. 
Thanks very much in advance
Ben

rsfcode <- nimbleCode({
  # Random Effects for each WMU
  for(w in 1:n.wmu){
    beta0[w] ~ dnorm(0, tau.b0)
    beta1[w] ~ dnorm(0, tau.b1)
    # individual random effects
    for(i in 1:n_deer){
      ind.beta0[w,i] ~ dnorm(beta0[WMU[i]], ind.tau.b0)
      ind.beta1[w,i] ~ dnorm(beta1[WMU[i]], ind.tau.b1)
      gamma[i] ~ dnorm(0,tau.gamma)
    }
  }
  # wmu level taus
  tau.b0 ~ dinvgamma(1,1)
  tau.b1 ~ dinvgamma(1,1)
  # individual level taus
  ind.tau.b0 ~ dinvgamma(1,1)
  ind.tau.b1 ~ dinvgamma(1,1)
  tau.gamma ~ dinvgamma(1,1)
  # likelihood model
  for (i in 1:n_deer) {
    # number of observations for each individual deer (used and available)
    for(j in 1:nobs[i]){
      used[j,i] ~ dbern(p[j,i])
      log(p[j,i]) <- ind.beta0[WMU[i],i] + ind.beta1[WMU[i],i] * x[j,i] + gamma[i]
    }
  }
})



mod.constants <- list(used = used,
                      x = can,
                      nobs = nobs.deer,  # the number of observations (used and avail) for each deer
                      n_deer = length(unique(btd.rsf$DeerID)),
                      n.wmu = length(unique(btd.rsf$WMU)),
                      WMU = wmu.numer)
str(mod.constants)

                  beta0 = rnorm(mod.constants$n_deer,0,5),
                  sigma_RE = runif(1,-5,5))
mod <- nimbleModel(code = rsfcode,

                   inits = mod.inits)

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: nimbleModel() run time
parts:
Hi Ben,
Thanks for the questions.
It looks like the warning about multiple definitions for gamma[i] is occurring because the declaration for gamma[i] is also nested within a for-loop for w. The BUGS model language is declarative, so it doesn't matter in what order declarations occur but once something is declared it can't be re-used or declared again. The solution to this is to write another for(i in 1:n_deer) loop outside of the w loop and declare gamma[i] inside that for loop.
The calculate step of nimbleModel is for diagnostic purposes, is not necessary, and can be very slow because everything is executing in R, and in an extra slow way to manage the model. The easiest way to skip this is "calculate=FALSE". Of course, then you don't get the benefit of the diagnostics, but you can proceed with further steps. Often it works well to let the diagnostic calculations run on a smaller toy model to check ideas and then scale up to a larger model with calculate=FALSE.
HTH
Perry

Hi Perry, 
Thanks for your quick response. I did as suggested, moving gamma into a separate for loop and setting calculate to FALSE and got things running more quickly. I think you are right that I should have begun things with a smaller set of data, but things do appear to be going forward warning free for the moment! 
I genuinely appreciate the time you and the rest of the nimble team put in to reviewing and responding to all of the questions here in the google group. I am sure it is a lot of work that probably isnt even part of your 'real' work. Thank you for that! 

Ben
